subject: Post-demo: SDK wiring, auth & structured-output next steps
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightpath.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-23T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo follow-up + what we need for a quickstart

Olga — thanks again for the demo this morning. Team found the latency/cost tradeoff examples helpful. A few follow-ups from our side so we can get an internal PoC moving this week:

- Can you share a minimal SDK quickstart for both Python and TypeScript (local, no cloud required) that shows: auth (API key + note on private/VPC option), a structured output example (tool-calling / JSON schema enforcement), and a short embeddings -> reranker flow?
- We’d like short commands we can run locally (pip/npm install, a curl example) and an example repo with sample apps we can fork.
- Security folks asked for your SOC/Security questionnaire back and where we can upload it.

Also: our technical PM (pm@brightpath.ai) would like to join a 60-minute deep-dive next week to align on the mutual action plan. Proposed times below.

Thanks —
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Integrations
BrightPath Health
[attachment: brightpath-security-questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)]
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightpath.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-23T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up + what we need for a quickstart

Sarah — great to meet you earlier, really appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and next steps below. I’ve attached a short quickstart guide and a draft mutual action plan (MAP) for your procurement loop.

High-level plan (what we’ll deliver by EOW):
1) SDK quickstart (attached) — two folders: /python and /ts. Each contains:
   - install steps (pip install redwood-inference, npm i @redwood/inference)
   - local run commands (env file with REDWOOD_API_KEY, minimal serverless sample)
   - curl + SDK sample to generate text and stream responses

2) Auth options explained:
   - Hosted/quick: API key (suitable for PoC) — show example using REDWOOD_API_KEY in env var.
   - Dedicated/Private: OAuth2 client credentials or mTLS with customer KMS. We’ll include a short OAuth snippet and notes for on-prem installs.

3) Structured outputs & tool calling:
   - Example schema enforcement via response_format (JSON schema) + a small tool-calling stub demonstrating how to surface supplier lookup results as a structured object.
   - Included sample: /python/samples/tool_calling_example.py — shows recommended prompt + structured output parser.

4) Embeddings + reranker flow:
   - Short pipeline: embed query -> nearest-neighbors over vector index -> rerank top-k with a 2nd-pass generation call.
   - Cost note: embeddings + reranker will be roughly X tokens for prep + Y tokens per rerank call; we’ll put concrete numbers for your sample dataset after we see a small prompt set.

Local smoke commands (from quickstart):
- Python: python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate && pip install -r python/requirements.txt
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxx
- python python/samples/run_text_gen.py
- TypeScript: cd ts && npm ci && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxx && npm run start:local
- curl example: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"Hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (contains code snippets), MAP-BrightPath.xlsx (draft timeline + owners). I uploaded the security questionnaire you sent to a shared folder and included the link below so your SecOps can retrieve it.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll drop the repo link and quickstart into the shared Drive by EOW.
- Kar thik will own a workshop for your devs (60 min) — he’ll include an embeddings/reranker walkthrough and a short cost/throughput section.
- Marissa will follow up on procurement timing and preferred contract flow.

Available times for the deep-dive: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT, Thu 2–4 PT. Let me know what works and I’ll calendar invite.

Cheers,

—
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (text/markdown)]
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightpath.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: pm@brightpath.ai
Date: 2028-04-23T20:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up + what we need for a quickstart

Thanks Olga — sounds good. We can do Wed 11:00 PT for the deep-dive; I’ll confirm with our PM. A couple quick clarifications before the workshop so we can prep:

- Can you add a short note in the quickstart about the reranker token-cost model (what you called X/Y above) with a concrete example for top-5 rerank on a 256-token context? Our finance folks like sample numbers.
- For private deployments: our infra team prefers KMS/HSM integration and an OAuth flow — will your sample include a stub for client-credentials and a note on key rotation?

PM and I will try the Python sample tomorrow and will reply with any immediate blockers.

Appreciate it —
Sarah
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-24T09:22:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-demo follow-up + what we need for a quickstart

Olga — I’ll own the hands-on workshop and the detailed runbook. Quick note I’m adding to the repo before the Wed deep-dive: a short runbook.md that includes
- explicit token-cost example for top-5 rerank with 256-token contexts (we’ll show numbers for 8-bit quantized v2 vs float16),
- an OAuth client-credentials snippet for Dedicated/Private with a reminder about rotating client secrets every 90 days,
- a tiny local example that uses FAISS-based vectors (python/sample_index.ipynb) and a TS reranker wrapper.

I’ll upload everything to the repo and link it to the Drive folder this afternoon.

—Karthik
Senior Developer Advocate
Redwood Inference
